### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. arrhythmogenic right ventricular dysplasia 9  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.464)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-6809371)

**Proposed mechanism:** Desmoplakin (HGNC:2722) —DISRUPTS→ Desmosome assembly and maintenance; Plakophilin 2 (HGNC:9020) —DISRUPTS→ Desmosome assembly and maintenance; Desmosome assembly and maintenance —LEADS_TO→ Cardiac cardiomyocyte adhesion; Cardiac cardiomyocyte adhesion —LEADS_TO→ Myocardial fibrosis (HP:0003071); Myocardial fibrosis (HP:0003071) —LEADS_TO→ Arrhythmia (HP:0011675). Loss-of-function mutations in either DSP (ARVD8) or PKP2 (ARVD9) disrupt the assembly and maintenance of cardiac desmosomes. This disruption impairs cardiomyocyte adhesion, leading to myocardial fibrosis and ultimately arrhythmogenic events.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of patients with pathogenic variants in DSP or PKP2 who do not exhibit any cardiac abnormalities or fibrosis, or conversely, identification of patients with ARVD8 or ARVD9 who have a completely distinct molecular pathway driving their disease phenotype unrelated to desmosomal function. _(variant: Exclusion of common variants (AF > 0.01) in DSP and PKP2 from pathogenic databases if they were to be implicated as the sole drivers of these rare diseases.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of DSP and PKP2 in ARVD8 and ARVD9 highlights the desmosome as a critical therapeutic target. Strategies aimed at stabilizing desmosomal function or mitigating the downstream effects of desmosome dysfunction, such as fibrosis, could be beneficial for patients with either form of the disease.
